overview: The Committee of the Whole conducted its fourth preliminary budget hearing for Fiscal Year 2027, reviewing the departments for Assessing, Facilities, Debt Service, Pensions, and Insurance.

items.title: Assessing Department Budget
items.summary: Chief Assessor Jared Yagjian presented a level-funded budget focused on promoting senior exemptions and expressed interest in future software for aerial growth detection.

items.title: Facilities Department Budget
items.summary: Director David McIntyre outlined a plan to transition to preventative maintenance to reduce long-term costs and discussed rising utility rates and custodial contract standards.

items.title: Bonds and Interest
items.summary: CFO Bob Dickinson reported a $1 million interest payment on temporary notes for school HVAC projects and noted the city's debt service remains at approximately 5% of the general fund.

items.title: Pensions
items.summary: Dickinson stated the city is on track to fully fund pension obligations by 2033, though the separate liability for retiree health insurance remains unfunded.

items.title: Workers' Compensation
items.summary: HR Director Lisa Crowley and CFO Bob Dickinson addressed a nearly 20% increase in the workers' compensation budget driven by rising medical evaluation costs and permanent disability claims.

items.title: Insurance Budget
items.summary: The committee reviewed a 9% increase in insurance costs primarily due to GIC healthcare rates and expanded Medicare costs for school employees. The matter was kept in committee.

subject: FY 2027 Preliminary Budget Hearings
